To mitigate Pakistan's vulnerability to climate change and disaster management, Pakistan Space Agency, SPARCO, hosts the UN SPIDER Regional Support Office, established National Disaster Risk Management Fund to develop the natural catastrophe model. This platform utilizes geo-reference data to project climate and disaster risk down to the sub-district level. Building on this, Pakistan recently launched the Space for Climate initiative. Its core is a geo-AI-enabled climate observatory that consolidates the satellite data and geospatial analytics to monitor atmospheric pollutants, greenhouse gases, and receding glaciers, directly advancing Pakistan's climate agenda. We are in the process of finalizing National Spatial Data Infrastructure to integrate multi-temporal satellite imagery directly into our government's 5-year development plan for evidence-based policymaking. Mr. Chair, Pakistan has significantly expanded its operational and remote sensing capabilities through successive orbital milestones. Drones.
